topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The Library vs. The Filing Cabinet
lecture_lines: Transformers have two distinct memory types.
Attention is your working memory.
The MLP acts as long-term memory.
MLPs store facts in synaptic weights.
It is like a internal brain database.
animations: Display two boxes: 'Attention' (left) and 'MLP' (right) with labels.
Animate 'Attention' as a flickering spotlight over scattered text blocks.
Animate 'MLP' as a static, glowing grid with fixed patterns.
Show the 'Attention' box fading in intensity while the 'MLP' becomes solid and vibrant.
Highlight both labels, establishing them as the 'Working' and 'Static' memory.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Neuron as a Pattern Matcher
lecture_lines: A neuron acts as a pattern matcher.
It detects specific features in data.
Weights determine the neuron's sensitivity.
animations: Display an Input Vector (green, #00FF00) approaching a node labeled 'Neuron'.
Show a Weight Matrix (blue, #0000FF) interacting with the Input Vector.
Animate the 'Neuron' node flashing bright yellow (#FFFF00) when the pattern matches.

sections.title: Mechanism: Key-Value Memory Networks
lecture_lines: MLPs function as Key-Value memories.
Keys detect the incoming input prompt.
Values project the specific output answer.
This bridges prompts to factual answers.
Like a lock finding its key.
animations: Draw a Key (lock shape) and a Value (key shape) side-by-side.
Display the Key interacting with a 'Prompt' vector, causing the lock to open.
Show the Value vector being projected into a space, resulting in the label 'Paris'.

sections.title: Visualization: The Fact-Retrieval Process
lecture_lines: Information flows through the network layers.
Weights activate to match patterns.
Facts emerge from these weight connections.
Retrieval is a distributed process.
Not one neuron holds the fact.
animations: Display a chain of nodes: Input Token -> MLP Layer -> Output Token.
Animate pulses moving through the MLP Layer nodes.
Highlight multiple connections spreading throughout the layer to show 'distributed' storage.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: MLPs are vast distributed databases.
Training saves facts into weights.
We can surgically update these weights.
animations: Visualize the MLP as a vast, 3D grid of weights (dots).
Show a 'surgical' edit on a specific cluster of weights (changing color).
Final overlay: 'MLP: A Distributed Knowledge Base'.
